newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Tuesday due to a fall on Shanghai's domestic A share market, which prompted funds to return to the repo markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day fell to 11.00 percent from 11.65 percent on Monday.
But the rate for three-day contract rose to 13.39 percent to 11.00 percent due the listing of Qinghai Tongren Aluminium Industrial Co, traders said.
Turnover fell to 6.34 million lots from 8.25 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the rates would continue to be affected by the volatile A share market in the next few days. Shanghai's A share index lost 1.86 percent to 976.227 points on Tuesday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Tuesday after dropping sharply in the past few trading days.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose slightly to 122.76 yuan from 122.50 yuan. Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 919,228 lots from 1.18 million.
Traders expect the market to continue to be weak in the short term with falling inflation depressing returns of state debt and consequently T-bill spot yields.
